# Palazzo

Self-hosted internet radio station controller — REST API to push songs, jingles, and live audio into a Liquidsoap/Icecast stream.

Single Docker container: NestJS + Liquidsoap + Icecast2.

## Quick Start

```bash
cp .env.example .env
docker network create broadcast-control 2>/dev/null || true
docker compose up -d
```

API: `http://localhost:3100` — Stream: `http://localhost:8000/stream`

## API

Automation clients should use the private program-scoped surface in
[Program-scoped playout](docs/program-playout.md). It provides atomic
song-plus-intro playout, program-scoped instant/mixer/state/event routes,
durable idempotency, and explicit intro lifecycle reporting.

Push a song: `POST /song` with `{"url": "https://...mp3"}`

All endpoints at a glance:

| Method | Path                                       | Description                                               |
| ------ | ------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `GET`  | `/status`                                  | Stream health and metadata                                |
| `GET`  | `/playback/state`                          | Authoritative current playback snapshot                   |
| `GET`  | `/playback/events`                         | Replay-safe Server-Sent Events                            |
| `GET`  | `/metrics`                                 | Private Prometheus telemetry                              |
| `GET`  | `/v1/programs/:programId/automation`       | Private automation lifecycle state                        |
| `POST` | `/v1/programs/:programId/automation/start` | Start the program automation without restarting transport |
| `POST` | `/v1/programs/:programId/automation/stop`  | Clear program material while preserving the Icecast mount |
| `PUT`  | `/v1/programs/:programId/fillers/:version` | Prepare immutable local radio filler from private Alcantara input |
| `GET`  | `/v1/programs/:programId/fillers/:version` | Read filler readiness without exposing signed source data |
| `POST` | `/song`                                    | Push a song, skips current                                |
| `POST` | `/song/stop`                               | Skip current song                                         |
| `POST` | `/instant`                                 | Push a jingle/SFX                                         |
| `POST` | `/instant/stop`                            | Stop all instants                                         |
| `GET`  | `/v1/programs/:programId/output/audio` | Return the configured Icecast audio on the private API |
| `GET`  | `/mixer`                                   | Read the applied song, instant, and main mixer state      |
| `PUT`  | `/mixer`                                   | Apply song, instant, and main volume/mute controls        |
| `GET`  | `/proxy-audio?url=`                        | CORS proxy for audio URLs                                 |

`POST /song` and `POST /instant` accept an optional caller-supplied
`playbackRequestId`, generating one when omitted. Song metadata and that ID
travel with the Liquidsoap request and reappear in lifecycle,
position, and state telemetry. Level samples are emitted at no more than 10 Hz,
position at 1 Hz, and heartbeats approximately every 10 seconds.

The control API, SSE feed, metrics, and Liquidsoap command socket are private
interfaces. The provided Compose and deployment mappings bind
the API to host loopback and join the private `broadcast-control` network;
publish only Icecast (or route it through a reverse proxy) for listeners.
On Cumulus, nginx exposes the same stream at `palazzo.gaulatti.com` and the
Modo Italiano listener hostname `radio.modoitaliano.fm`; the latter redirects
its root to `/stream` and includes the public CORS header used by radio clients.

Container application logs use Docker's host-local `local` driver, bounded to
three 10 MB files per container. Operators can inspect them with
`docker logs --tail 200 palazzo`; Palazzo does not send application logs to
CloudWatch.

For a failed Cumulus deployment, the GitHub Actions job shows SSM remote stdout
and stderr as separate lines and annotates the remote exit code. A missing
deployment token is reported by name without showing its value.

Palazzo boots in `reconciliation-required`: container or process startup never
pretends a prior operator Start/Stop succeeded. Alcantara reconciles it through
the private lifecycle API. Start becomes ready only when Liquidsoap, its
control/telemetry connection, and the Icecast source output are healthy. Stop
flushes both queues and waits for authoritative idle while leaving Liquidsoap
and the 24x7 Icecast mount connected. See
[docs/broadcast-lifecycle.md](docs/broadcast-lifecycle.md).

Full details: [API Reference](wiki/API-Reference)

Telemetry operations and migration guidance:
[docs/playback-telemetry.md](docs/playback-telemetry.md).

## Pull request verification

Local agent review is installed and updated from public Clouseau through the
bastille startup bootstrap. It uses the developer's authenticated Codex or
Claude account and `.clouseau-local.json`; it requires no CI provider keys.
Before creating any PR, agents must run the shared `clouseau` skill, resolve its
findings and rerun after repairs against the final committed change. Publish the
passing signed receipt in the initial ready PR body. `AGENTS.md` owns this rule;
`CLAUDE.md` points Claude Code to it. Never push directly to `main`.
See [local review](https://github.com/gaulatti/clouseau/blob/main/docs/local-review.md).

Every PR runs unit tests with exact 100% line and branch coverage over all
application sources, type-checking, the production dependency audit, workflow
security tests, and real Liquidsoap/Icecast container checks. Run
`npm run test:coverage` locally with Node 22.22.0 and ffmpeg/ffprobe installed.
Native c8 reports include unloaded bootstrap/module files; Clouseau independently
checks the complete source inventory and exact counters.

After those checks pass, a PR carrying an authenticated local review stamp uses
the pinned verifier without AI credentials or an AI rerun. The verifier checks
the enrolled GitHub author, signature, exact source/base, engine and policy,
expiry, literal evidence and calculated scores. Invalid stamps hold approval
without invoking a paid reviewer. Only a protected owner change can enroll or
revoke a workstation key. The enrolled workstation and its privileged processes
are trusted; this is not hardware attestation.

PRs without a stamp retain the separately installed CI reviewer. It assesses purpose, need,
proportionality, technical findings and test integrity. Jev grades its qualified
narrow factors; independent DeepSeek reviews handle the remaining questions.
Passing reviews receive a bot approval and native auto-merge under main's branch
protection. Unresolved product-direction decisions go to gaulatti. Intent
confirmation never waives tests, coverage or integrity. See
[the purpose contract](.github/clouseau.md) and
[Continuous Verification](https://github.com/gaulatti/palazzo/wiki/Continuous-Verification).

Verification and AI review run separately: metadata reassessment does not rebuild
the container, and provider calls wait for real verification to finish. A bot
merge explicitly dispatches the existing deployment workflow for runtime changes;
deployment completion and live stream health remain separate checks.

Protected reviewer installation runs only from the owner-pushed
`policy-install/pr-N` branch at the exact ready PR head, after its matching
`/approve-intent` confirmation. It reuses the PR's independent technical checks
and performs fresh AI assessment before the native approval gate. Manual
dispatch is for verification or reassessment: GitHub excludes dispatched job
checks from required PR checks, so it cannot install the reviewer.

## Documentation

After the `Deploy` workflow succeeds on main, `Maintain deployed wiki` uses
Clouseau to plan every affected page, generate it and independently fact-check
its source citations. It publishes the validated pages together in one non-force
wiki commit. The wiki receipt records the actual deployed source and deployment
run; documentation does not close tickets or claim live service health.

Generation has read-only GitHub access and the model key. Publication has wiki
write access and no model or deployment key. Both stages verify the successful
main deployment again and reject a superseded release; publication also rejects
concurrent human wiki edits. Source is read as text from an explicit public
allowlist. Failed deployments cannot start documentation generation.

For catch-up, the repository owner can dispatch `wiki.yml` with `deployment_run`
set to the latest successful `deploy.yml` run. This generates and publishes docs
for that verified deployed revision without starting a deployment. Repeating an
already documented source is idempotent and makes no model call.

## Program audio return

Alcántara monitors the encoded output through
`GET /v1/programs/:programId/output/audio`. Palazzo connects only to its own
configured `ICECAST_PORT`/`ICECAST_MOUNT` on loopback, preserving content type
and forwarding bytes incrementally. This private program-scoped endpoint needs
no public listener hostname. Closing the client closes the Icecast connection
without changing broadcast playback. See the wiki API Reference for errors and
monitor metrics.

Production dependency verification uses `npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=high`.
The Fastify override pins 5.12.5 while keeping NestJS on version 11; remove or
update it only after the adapter resolves a patched version and the HTTP/runtime
gates pass. The unused Dockerode SDK is removed: Palazzo manages its Liquidsoap
child process directly. These dependency corrections preserve metric contracts.

# Palazzo review contract

Palazzo is a single-program internet-radio playout appliance: one container
combines a private NestJS/Fastify control API, Liquidsoap and Icecast. Alcantara
uses it to prepare immutable filler, play songs with optional recorded intros,
mix instants and live audio, observe authoritative playback, and maintain a
continuous listener stream.

Preserve program isolation, private control/telemetry interfaces, durable
idempotency before audible effects, bounded dependency retries and metric labels,
explicit Start/Stop reconciliation, actual media validation, and an uninterrupted
Icecast mount. Command acceptance is not proof of playback; engine observations
and real output bytes establish that result. Startup never invents a prior
operator Start or Stop.

Assess purpose and evidence rather than the number of changed files or lines.
Bug fixes, meaningful tests that raise coverage, dependency repairs, and
operational maintenance can serve this existing appliance without a new product
decision. Browser access to existing private controls, protocol correctness,
recovery, media validation and accurate telemetry are established obligations.
New capabilities must have repository documentation or linked acceptance criteria
that establish their actual need and boundaries.

Ask gaulatti for a second opinion for a product-direction or authority decision:
for example turning the appliance into a content-generation platform, a general
CMS, a multi-tenant hosting service, or a publicly exposed control system.
Ordinary implementation uncertainty and repairable bugs belong to automated
investigation, not routine human code review. Changes to review controls,
coverage exclusions, or this purpose contract require explicit owner confirmation.

Every material capability and mechanism must independently score at least 80 for
fit, need and proportionality under Clouseau's shared protocol. A causal technical
finding at or above 70 blocks; unrelated features or good scores cannot average
away a defect. Integrity and review-completeness gates remain independent.

Tests must assert actual production behavior and failure outcomes. Reject
fabricated coverage, disabled tests, swallowed errors, unconditional assertions,
test-only readiness paths and mocks that replace the behavior being claimed.
External socket, subprocess and filesystem fault injection is legitimate when
the real application contract and failure handling remain exercised. The pinned
container must separately prove real ffmpeg preparation, Liquidsoap control,
Icecast output bytes, lifecycle reconciliation and parsed bounded metrics.

All tests and exactly 100% application line and branch coverage remain mandatory
for every contribution, including external forks. Unloaded bootstrap and module
files must be measured. Missing or unresolved integrity evidence holds approval;
intent confirmation cannot waive it. Contributor code never receives provider,
repair or approval credentials, and fork PRs cannot trigger automatic repairs.

Clouseau owns the shared scoring, investigation, repair bounds, evidence ledger,
native approval and auto-merge. This repository owns its purpose, real tests and
runtime evidence. CI/merge, deployment completion and live health are separate
milestones; a successful merge alone is not a deployment or playback claim.

A passing local Clouseau review may be reused only through a signed receipt from
an enrolled trusted workstation and the matching native GitHub author. CI must
independently verify current protected policy, exact head/base and engine content,
expiry, evidence and deterministic scores. This route has no AI credentials and
must not fall back to paid review when verification fails. All native tests,
exact coverage, container checks and branch protections remain mandatory.
Agent installation and account-authenticated local execution remain independent
of CI enrollment and CI provider keys. A signature authenticates the workstation;
it does not attest against compromise of that workstation or its operator.

name: Palazzo CI
run-name: >-
  ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && format('Verify PR #{0}', github.event.pull_request.number) ||
      inputs.check_author && 'Verify repair author' ||
      (github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'Verify main' ||
      format('PR review ({0})', github.event.pull_request.number || github.event.issue.number || inputs.pull_request || github.ref_name) }}
on:
  push:
    branches: [main, 'policy-install/**']
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, ready_for_review]
  pull_request_target:
    branches: [main]
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, ready_for_review, edited]
  issue_comment:
    types: [created]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      pull_request:
        description: PR number to reassess without executing contributor code; empty runs verification
        type: string
        required: false
      check_author:
        description: Inspect existing repair author identity and repository access without writing or deploying
        type: boolean
        default: false
permissions:
  contents: read
concurrency:
  group: palazzo-ci-${{ github.event_name }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.event.issue.number || inputs.pull_request || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true
jobs:
  unit:
    if: &verify-code >-
      github.event_name == 'pull_request' || (github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') ||
      (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.pull_request == '' && !inputs.check_author)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    outputs:
      wiki_tests_passed: ${{ steps.workflow-tests.outputs.wiki_tests_passed }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22.22.0
          cache: npm
      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci
      - name: Ensure local media test tools
        run: |
          if ! command -v ffmpeg >/dev/null || ! command -v ffprobe >/dev/null; then
            sudo apt-get update
            sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends ffmpeg
          fi
      - name: Test application with complete source coverage
        run: npm run test:coverage
      - name: Type-check
        run: npm run typecheck
      - name: Audit production dependencies
        run: npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=high
      - name: Test approval policy
        uses: gaulatti/clouseau@c88bb23a03c35f703f86ad1c419b80e390a07f03
        with:
          operation: test
      - name: Check out pinned reviewer for consumer integration tests
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          repository: gaulatti/clouseau
          ref: c88bb23a03c35f703f86ad1c419b80e390a07f03
          path: .clouseau-ci
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Test workflow routing
        id: workflow-tests
        run: |
          test -f .github/tests/wiki-workflow.test.mjs
          npm ci --prefix .github/tests --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund
          npm test --prefix .github/tests
          echo 'wiki_tests_passed=true' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - name: Retain native application coverage
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: application-coverage-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: |
            coverage/coverage-final.json
            coverage/coverage-summary.json
            coverage/lcov.info
          if-no-files-found: error

  verify:
    name: >-
      ${{ (github.event_name == 'pull_request' || (github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') ||
          (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.pull_request == '' && !inputs.check_author)) && 'verify' || 'metadata-only' }}
    needs: [unit, container]
    if: always()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - name: Require passing unit and real radio runtime checks
        if: >-
          always() && (github.event_name == 'pull_request' || (github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') ||
          (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.pull_request == '' && !inputs.check_author))
        env:
          UNIT_RESULT: ${{ needs.unit.result }}
          RUNTIME_RESULT: ${{ needs.container.result }}
        run: test "$UNIT_RESULT" = success && test "$RUNTIME_RESULT" = success
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        if: *verify-code
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Load this run's native coverage report
        if: *verify-code
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: application-coverage-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: coverage
      - name: Enforce 100% line and branch coverage
        if: *verify-code
        uses: gaulatti/clouseau@c88bb23a03c35f703f86ad1c419b80e390a07f03
        with:
          operation: coverage
          coverage-format: istanbul
          coverage-report: coverage/coverage-final.json
          source-directory: src
      - name: Require wiki-workflow.test.mjs execution
        if: *verify-code
        env:
          WIKI_TESTS_PASSED: ${{ needs.unit.outputs.wiki_tests_passed }}
        run: test "$WIKI_TESTS_PASSED" = true

  container:
    if: *verify-code
    timeout-minutes: 20
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22.22.0

      - name: Build pinned runtime image
        run: docker build --build-arg BUILD_VERSION=${{ github.sha }} --tag palazzo:ci .

      - name: Test real media preparation in pinned runtime
        run: |
          docker run --rm \
            --entrypoint node \
            --volume "$PWD/test:/workspace/test:ro" \
            --env PALAZZO_DIST_DIR=/app/dist \
            palazzo:ci \
            --test /workspace/test/runtime/filler-store.service.test.js

      - name: Start and verify pinned runtime
        run: bash test/runtime/verify-station.sh

  assess-intent:
    if: &review-event >-
      (github.event_name == 'pull_request_target' && !github.event.pull_request.draft) ||
      (github.event_name == 'push' && !github.event.deleted && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/heads/policy-install/'))
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 70
    permissions:
      actions: read
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
      issues: read
    outputs:
      assessment: ${{ steps.local-review.outputs.assessment || steps.assess.outputs.assessment }}
      number: ${{ steps.install.outputs.number || github.event.pull_request.number }}
    steps:
      - name: Verify the owner-authorized frozen reviewer installation
        if: github.event_name == 'push'
        id: install
        uses: actions/github-script@v7
        with:
          script: |
            const match = context.ref.match(/^refs\/heads\/policy-install\/pr-([1-9][0-9]*)$/);
            if (context.actor !== context.repo.owner || !/^[a-f0-9]{40}$/.test(context.sha) || !match) {
              throw new Error('Reviewer installation requires the repository owner and a ready PR number');
            }
            const pull_number = Number(match[1]);
            if (!Number.isSafeInteger(pull_number)) throw new Error('Invalid installation PR number');
            const {data: pr} = await github.rest.pulls.get({...context.repo, pull_number});
            if (pr.state !== 'open' || pr.draft || pr.base.ref !== 'main' ||
                pr.user.login !== context.repo.owner || pr.head.sha !== context.sha ||
                pr.head.repo?.full_name !== `${context.repo.owner}/${context.repo.repo}`) {
              throw new Error('Installation requires the owner-authored same-repository PR at this exact workflow revision');
            }
            const comments = await github.paginate(github.rest.issues.listComments,
              {...context.repo, issue_number: pull_number, per_page: 100});
            if (!comments.some(comment => comment.user?.type === 'User' && comment.user.login === context.repo.owner &&
                comment.body.trim() === `/approve-intent ${context.sha}`)) {
              throw new Error('Installation requires owner intent confirmation at this exact revision');
            }
            core.setOutput('number', String(pull_number));
      # Never load the controller or its configuration from the PR.
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: main
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Check out the pinned trusted verification reader
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          repository: gaulatti/clouseau
          ref: c88bb23a03c35f703f86ad1c419b80e390a07f03
          path: .clouseau-review
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Wait for tests, exact coverage, and real radio runtime
        uses: actions/github-script@v7
        env:
          REQUESTED_PR: ${{ steps.install.outputs.number }}
        with:
          script: |
            const path = require('node:path');
            const root = path.resolve('.clouseau-review');
            const config = require(path.join(root, 'src/config.cjs')).loadConfig('.github/clouseau.json');
            const policy = require(path.join(root, 'src/policy.cjs')).createPolicy(config);
            const number = context.payload.pull_request?.number || Number(process.env.REQUESTED_PR);
            for (let attempt = 0; attempt < 120; attempt++) {
              const {data: pr} = await github.rest.pulls.get({...context.repo, pull_number: number});
              const expected = context.payload.pull_request?.head.sha || context.sha;
              if (pr.state !== 'open' || pr.draft || pr.head.sha !== expected) {
                throw new Error('PR closed, became draft, or changed while verification was pending');
              }
              const result = await policy.technicalRun(github, context.repo, pr);
              if (result.failure) throw new Error(result.failure);
              if (!result.pending) { core.info(`Verified PR CI: ${result.url}. Clouseau acceptance can now start.`); return; }
              core.info('Waiting for independent unit/coverage and Liquidsoap/Icecast checks. No AI request has been made.');
              await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 15000));
            }
            throw new Error('PR verification did not complete within 30 minutes');
      - name: Select authenticated local review or the installed CI reviewer
        id: review-route
        uses: actions/github-script@v7
        with:
          script: |
            core.setOutput('local', String((context.payload.pull_request?.body || '').includes('clouseau-local-review:v1')));
      - name: Verify authenticated local review without AI credentials
        if: steps.review-route.outputs.local == 'true'
        id: local-review
        uses: gaulatti/clouseau@c88bb23a03c35f703f86ad1c419b80e390a07f03
        with:
          operation: verify-local
          pull-request: ${{ steps.install.outputs.number }}
          wait-for-verification: 'false'
      - name: Review unstamped PR through the installed CI AI reviewer
        if: steps.review-route.outputs.local != 'true'
        uses: gaulatti/clouseau@c88bb23a03c35f703f86ad1c419b80e390a07f03
        id: assess
        with:
          operation: assess
          pull-request: ${{ steps.install.outputs.number }}
          wait-for-verification: 'false'
          provider-key: ${{ secrets.DEEPSEEK_API_KEY }}
          typesafe-key: ${{ secrets.TYPESAFE_API_KEY }}
      - name: Retain acceptance record
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: clouseau-acceptance-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: work/clouseau-acceptance*.json
          if-no-files-found: ignore

  approve-and-merge:
    name: ${{ ((github.event_name == 'pull_request_target' && !github.event.pull_request.draft) || (github.event_name == 'push' && !github.event.deleted && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/heads/policy-install/'))) && 'approve-and-merge' || 'metadata-only-approval' }}
    needs: assess-intent
    # Always resolve the job name; only trusted, ready PR events run its steps.
    # A failed assessment must still fail the required native approval check.
    if: always()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: write
      pull-requests: write
      issues: write
      actions: write
    concurrency:
      group: pr-approval-${{ needs.assess-intent.outputs.number || github.run_id }}
      cancel-in-progress: false
    steps:
      - name: Require a completed assessment
        if: >-
          ((github.event_name == 'pull_request_target' && !github.event.pull_request.draft) ||
          (github.event_name == 'push' && !github.event.deleted && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/heads/policy-install/'))) &&
          needs.assess-intent.result != 'success'
        run: exit 1
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        if: *review-event
        with:
          ref: main
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Load this run's acceptance record
        if: >-
          ((github.event_name == 'pull_request_target' && !github.event.pull_request.draft) ||
          (github.event_name == 'push' && !github.event.deleted && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/heads/policy-install/'))) &&
          needs.assess-intent.result == 'success' &&
          fromJSON(needs.assess-intent.outputs.assessment).record_digest != ''
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: clouseau-acceptance-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: work
      - if: *review-event
        uses: gaulatti/clouseau@c88bb23a03c35f703f86ad1c419b80e390a07f03
        with:
          operation: gate
          pull-request: ${{ needs.assess-intent.outputs.number }}
          native-gate: 'true'
          assessment: ${{ needs.assess-intent.outputs.assessment }}

  apply-repair:
    needs: [assess-intent, approve-and-merge]
    if: >-
      always() && github.event_name == 'pull_request_target' && !github.event.pull_request.draft &&
      github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository &&
      needs.assess-intent.result == 'success' && needs.approve-and-merge.result == 'failure' &&
      fromJSON(needs.assess-intent.outputs.assessment).repair_digest != ''
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      issues: write
      pull-requests: read
      actions: read
    concurrency:
      group: pr-approval-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
      cancel-in-progress: false
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: main
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: clouseau-acceptance-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: work
      - uses: gaulatti/clouseau@c88bb23a03c35f703f86ad1c419b80e390a07f03
        with:
          operation: repair
          assessment: ${{ needs.assess-intent.outputs.assessment }}
          repair-token: ${{ secrets.DEPLOYMENT_TOKEN }}

  finalize-merge:
    needs: [assess-intent, approve-and-merge]
    if: *review-event
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
      actions: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: main
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: gaulatti/clouseau@c88bb23a03c35f703f86ad1c419b80e390a07f03
        with:
          operation: finalize
          pull-request: ${{ needs.assess-intent.outputs.number }}
          assessment: ${{ needs.assess-intent.outputs.assessment }}

  request-reassessment:
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'issue_comment' && github.event.issue.pull_request && startsWith(github.event.comment.body, '/approve-intent ')) ||
      (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.pull_request != '' && !inputs.check_author)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 3
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
      actions: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: main
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: gaulatti/clouseau@c88bb23a03c35f703f86ad1c419b80e390a07f03
        with:
          operation: request-reassessment
          pull-request: ${{ inputs.pull_request }}

  check-author:
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.check_author
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 3
    permissions: {}
    steps:
      - name: Verify independent repair author without writing
        uses: actions/github-script@v7
        with:
          github-token: ${{ secrets.DEPLOYMENT_TOKEN }}
          script: |
            const {data: user} = await github.rest.users.getAuthenticated();
            const {data: repository} = await github.rest.repos.get(context.repo);
            if (user.login === 'github-actions[bot]' || !repository.permissions?.push) {
              throw new Error('Repair requires an independent author with Contents write access');
            }
            core.info(`Independent repair author ${user.login} can access ${context.repo.owner}/${context.repo.repo}. No write or deployment was made.`);

# Palazzo

Self-hosted internet radio station controller — REST API to push songs, jingles, and live audio into a Liquidsoap/Icecast stream.

Single Docker container: NestJS + Liquidsoap + Icecast2.

## Quick Start

```bash
cp .env.example .env
docker network create broadcast-control 2>/dev/null || true
docker compose up -d
```

API: `http://localhost:3100` — Stream: `http://localhost:8000/stream`

## API

Automation clients should use the private program-scoped surface in
[Program-scoped playout](docs/program-playout.md). It provides atomic
song-plus-intro playout, program-scoped instant/mixer/state/event routes,
durable idempotency, and explicit intro lifecycle reporting.

Push a song: `POST /song` with `{"url": "https://...mp3"}`

All endpoints at a glance:

| Method | Path                                       | Description                                               |
| ------ | ------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `GET`  | `/status`                                  | Stream health and metadata                                |
| `GET`  | `/playback/state`                          | Authoritative current playback snapshot                   |
| `GET`  | `/playback/events`                         | Replay-safe Server-Sent Events                            |
| `GET`  | `/metrics`                                 | Private Prometheus telemetry                              |
| `GET`  | `/v1/programs/:programId/automation`       | Private automation lifecycle state                        |
| `POST` | `/v1/programs/:programId/automation/start` | Start the program automation without restarting transport |
| `POST` | `/v1/programs/:programId/automation/stop`  | Clear program material while preserving the Icecast mount |
| `PUT`  | `/v1/programs/:programId/fillers/:version` | Prepare immutable local radio filler from private Alcantara input |
| `GET`  | `/v1/programs/:programId/fillers/:version` | Read filler readiness without exposing signed source data |
| `POST` | `/song`                                    | Push a song, skips current                                |
| `POST` | `/song/stop`                               | Skip current song                                         |
| `POST` | `/instant`                                 | Push a jingle/SFX                                         |
| `POST` | `/instant/stop`                            | Stop all instants                                         |
| `GET`  | `/v1/programs/:programId/output/audio` | Return the configured Icecast audio on the private API |
| `GET`  | `/mixer`                                   | Read the applied song, instant, and main mixer state      |
| `PUT`  | `/mixer`                                   | Apply song, instant, and main volume/mute controls        |
| `GET`  | `/proxy-audio?url=`                        | CORS proxy for audio URLs                                 |

`POST /song` and `POST /instant` accept an optional caller-supplied
`playbackRequestId`, generating one when omitted. Song metadata and that ID
travel with the Liquidsoap request and reappear in lifecycle,
position, and state telemetry. Level samples are emitted at no more than 10 Hz,
position at 1 Hz, and heartbeats approximately every 10 seconds.

The control API, SSE feed, metrics, and Liquidsoap command socket are private
interfaces. The provided Compose and deployment mappings bind
the API to host loopback and join the private `broadcast-control` network;
publish only Icecast (or route it through a reverse proxy) for listeners.
On Cumulus, nginx exposes the same stream at `palazzo.gaulatti.com` and the
Modo Italiano listener hostname `radio.modoitaliano.fm`; the latter redirects
its root to `/stream` and includes the public CORS header used by radio clients.

Container application logs use Docker's host-local `local` driver, bounded to
three 10 MB files per container. Operators can inspect them with
`docker logs --tail 200 palazzo`; Palazzo does not send application logs to
CloudWatch.

For a failed Cumulus deployment, the GitHub Actions job shows SSM remote stdout
and stderr as separate lines and annotates the remote exit code. A missing
deployment token is reported by name without showing its value.

Palazzo boots in `reconciliation-required`: container or process startup never
pretends a prior operator Start/Stop succeeded. Alcantara reconciles it through
the private lifecycle API. Start becomes ready only when Liquidsoap, its
control/telemetry connection, and the Icecast source output are healthy. Stop
flushes both queues and waits for authoritative idle while leaving Liquidsoap
and the 24x7 Icecast mount connected. See
[docs/broadcast-lifecycle.md](docs/broadcast-lifecycle.md).

Full details: [API Reference](wiki/API-Reference)

Telemetry operations and migration guidance:
[docs/playback-telemetry.md](docs/playback-telemetry.md).

## Pull request verification

Local agent review is installed and updated from public Clouseau through the
bastille startup bootstrap. It uses the developer's authenticated Codex or
Claude account and `.clouseau-local.json`; it requires no CI provider keys.
Before creating any PR, agents must run the shared `clouseau` skill, resolve its
findings and rerun after repairs against the final committed change. Publish the
passing signed receipt in the initial ready PR body. `AGENTS.md` owns this rule;
`CLAUDE.md` points Claude Code to it. Never push directly to `main`.
See [local review](https://github.com/gaulatti/clouseau/blob/main/docs/local-review.md).

Every PR runs unit tests with exact 100% line and branch coverage over all
application sources, type-checking, the production dependency audit, workflow
security tests, and real Liquidsoap/Icecast container checks. Run
`npm run test:coverage` locally with Node 22.22.0 and ffmpeg/ffprobe installed.
Native c8 reports include unloaded bootstrap/module files; Clouseau independently
checks the complete source inventory and exact counters.

After those checks pass, a PR carrying an authenticated local review stamp uses
the pinned verifier without AI credentials or an AI rerun. The verifier checks
the enrolled GitHub author, signature, exact source/base, engine and policy,
expiry, literal evidence and calculated scores. Invalid stamps hold approval
without invoking a paid reviewer. Only a protected owner change can enroll or
revoke a workstation key. The enrolled workstation and its privileged processes
are trusted; this is not hardware attestation.

PRs without a stamp retain the separately installed CI reviewer. It assesses purpose, need,
proportionality, technical findings and test integrity. Jev grades its qualified
narrow factors; independent DeepSeek reviews handle the remaining questions.
Passing reviews receive a bot approval and native auto-merge under main's branch
protection. Unresolved product-direction decisions go to gaulatti. Intent
confirmation never waives tests, coverage or integrity. See
[the purpose contract](.github/clouseau.md) and
[Continuous Verification](https://github.com/gaulatti/palazzo/wiki/Continuous-Verification).

Verification and AI review run separately: metadata reassessment does not rebuild
the container, and provider calls wait for real verification to finish. A bot
merge explicitly dispatches the existing deployment workflow for runtime changes;
deployment completion and live stream health remain separate checks.

Protected reviewer installation runs only from the owner-pushed
`policy-install/pr-N` branch at the exact ready PR head, after its matching
`/approve-intent` confirmation. It reuses the PR's independent technical checks
and performs fresh AI assessment before the native approval gate. Manual
dispatch is for verification or reassessment: GitHub excludes dispatched job
checks from required PR checks, so it cannot install the reviewer.

## Documentation

After the `Deploy` workflow succeeds on main, `Maintain deployed wiki` uses
Clouseau to plan every affected page, generate it and independently fact-check
its source citations. It publishes the validated pages together in one non-force
wiki commit. The wiki receipt records the actual deployed source and deployment
run; documentation does not close tickets or claim live service health.

Generation has read-only GitHub access and the model key. Publication has wiki
write access and no model or deployment key. Both stages verify the successful
main deployment again and reject a superseded release; publication also rejects
concurrent human wiki edits. Source is read as text from an explicit public
allowlist. Failed deployments cannot start documentation generation.

For catch-up, the repository owner can dispatch `wiki.yml` with `deployment_run`
set to the latest successful `deploy.yml` run. This generates and publishes docs
for that verified deployed revision without starting a deployment. Repeating an
already documented source is idempotent and makes no model call.

## Program audio return

Alcántara monitors the encoded output through
`GET /v1/programs/:programId/output/audio`. Palazzo connects only to its own
configured `ICECAST_PORT`/`ICECAST_MOUNT` on loopback, preserving content type
and forwarding bytes incrementally. This private program-scoped endpoint needs
no public listener hostname. Closing the client closes the Icecast connection
without changing broadcast playback. See the wiki API Reference for errors and
monitor metrics.

Production dependency verification uses `npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=high`.
The Fastify override pins 5.12.5 while keeping NestJS on version 11; remove or
update it only after the adapter resolves a patched version and the HTTP/runtime
gates pass. The unused Dockerode SDK is removed: Palazzo manages its Liquidsoap
child process directly. These dependency corrections preserve metric contracts.

See [automatic Clouseau CI upgrades](docs/automatic-ci-upgrades.md) for the trusted
central source, frozen engine identity, receipt compatibility and diagnostics.

# Automatic Clouseau CI upgrades

Source CI defines “latest” as the commit on protected `gaulatti/clouseau` main
when the isolated `resolve-clouseau` job runs. The pinned public bootstrap has no
repository or branch inputs. It validates protection and the full SHA, checks
out that immutable revision and computes its engine digest. Each engine job
uses those same outputs; a central advance affects the next run only.

Tests, receipt verification, AI review when needed, deterministic scores,
approval and merge use that frozen checkout. Unavailable, malformed or
unauthorized resolution blocks approval with no old-version fallback. Required
native check names, forks, Dependabot and credential separation stay unchanged.
Missing resolver output selects an invalid all-zero commit so checkout cannot
silently use its default branch.
Contributor execution receives no provider or write credentials.

Protected `.github/clouseau.json` authorizes the exact central source instead of
enrolling a new digest per release. Existing signer keys, author binding,
expiry and revocation stay repository-local. Proposed PR configuration cannot

Alcántara monitors the encoded output through

configured `ICECAST_PORT`/`ICECAST_MOUNT` on loopback, preserving content type

no public listener hostname. Closing the client closes the Icecast connection
without changing broadcast playback. See the wiki API Reference for errors and
monitor metrics.

# Palazzo

Self-hosted internet radio station controller — REST API to push songs, jingles, and live audio into a Liquidsoap/Icecast stream.

Single Docker container: NestJS + Liquidsoap + Icecast2.

## Quick Start

```bash
cp .env.example .env
docker network create broadcast-control 2>/dev/null || true
docker compose up -d
```
